narrative.intro: AMI Metals has $1.5B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. The company received 9 awards with an average award size of $164M. Obligations rose up 3016758.9% year over year, driven by a concentration of FY26 activity after minimal obligations in prior fiscal years. Fiscal-year obligations were $9.8K in FY21, $165K in FY22, $109K in FY23, $346K in FY24, $48.9K in FY25, and $1.5B in FY26. The Department of Homeland Security is the dominant buyer with $1.5B in obligations, while the Department of Defense recorded $13.5K. Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services is the largest market by obligations at $1.5B, followed by Other Support Activities for Air Transportation at $13.5K. Current-year totals are partial because figures are fiscal year to date. The award-value totals in the largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables are total contract values, while the rest of the figures are contract obligations.

sections.heading: How concentrated is AMI Metals' FY2026 federal revenue?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security accounted for $1.5B of AMI Metals' FY2026 obligations. The Department of Defense accounted for $13.5K, showing that fiscal-year activity is heavily concentrated in a single agency. Prior fiscal years show minimal obligations relative to FY26. The largest market is Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services at $1.5B.

sections.heading: How have AMI Metals' obligations trended over recent fiscal years?
sections.body: FY26 obligations were $1.5B compared with $48.9K in FY25 and smaller amounts in earlier years. Obligations were $9.8K in FY21, $165K in FY22, $109K in FY23, and $346K in FY24. The year-over-year change into FY26 was up 3016758.9%.
